title: Remembering democratic transitions, the (re-)building of democratic institutions, and strengthening society based on the rule of law, democracy, and fundamental rights.
description: Objective: 1. CERV-2026-CITIZENS-REM-TRANSITION - Remembering democratic transitions, the (re-)building of democratic institutions, and strengthening society based on the rule of law, democracy, and fundamental rights. The EU is a community of values, and all its Member States committed to respect the principles of democracy, the rule of law, and respect for fundamental rights . Europe's experiences in the 20th century demonstrates the need for resilient democracies and the need for people to actively engage in and protect democratic institutions and values. Historical experience such as in the 1920s and 1930s, when some European democracies went through particularly challenging times, are stark reminders of the importance to promote democracy, also in a historical perspective. Today, democracy faces several challenges, which underlined the need to strengthen public trust in democratic processes and institutions and to recall the importance of democracy in people’s daily life. Democratic transitions (defined as the transition from a non-democratic to a democratic system, a transition undertaken by several European countries before joining the EU) are not only political and legal processes but also societal transformations.The transition and consolidation of democracies through institutional and legal reforms have been essential. In addition, delivering justice to victims and affected communities after the fall of totalitarian and authoritarian regimes (including communist and fascist dictatorships) can aid in societal healing, bolster and reinforce resilience against present and future threats to democracies. Projects under this topic can focus on: The ongoing development and nurturing of democracies in the context of past transitions from authoritarian and totalitarian regimes (including communist and fascist dictatorships) across various European countries, reveals important lessons for defending and upholding EU values such as democracy, the rule of law, and fundamental rights. They can also reflect on both shared patterns and national specificities, while underlining the lasting impact of the totalitarian or authoritarian past, and how its difficult legacy continues to be remembered, interpreted, and engaged with today. Examining and giving visibility to acts of resistance and organised opposition to past totalitarian and authoritarian regimes, as part of the ongoing effort to nurture and protect democracy in the face of enduring and emerging challenges. Transition from authoritarian and totalitarian regimes (including communist and fascist dictatorships) towards democracy. Promoting remembrance and education about past events in which fundamental rights such as freedom of expression, assembly, thought, conscience, religion, and electoral rights were suppressed under past totalitarian and authoritarian regimes. These examples serve to reinforce the importance of protecting democratic values today, including the right to express dissenting opinions and ensuring a political space where opposition voices can be freely and safely heard. Exploring the means of historical justice, be it through trials, restitution or amnesty, and possibility still today to work on restorative justice. The elements described above to strengthen democracies, such as fighting foreign interference, including the manipulation and falsification of historical facts, strengthen citizen engagement, critical thinking, media literacy, and societal resilience, are closely related to the context of remembrance, as they help ensure that the dramatic events of the past are not repeated in contemporary Europe. For further information about the call and its conditions, please see the Call document .

eligibilityText: SMEs located in COSME countries, which are members of the project Clusters* or in a process of becoming members and that are interested in strengthening their international capacity in the target countries of F2F Health Matters and the following areas: i) Innovative & Sustainable Healthy Food, ii) Bio-based Techno-functional Ingredients & Solutions and iii) Bio-solutions -- to become more global across overseas markets of connected food, the market of functional food and healthy ingredient, the market of processed food products, can apply for support. An initial eligibility check will be conducted following the criteria established in the call. All applicants will be notified about the eligibility verification. Eligible applicants will be notified they have been shortlisted and will proceed to the evaluation step. The project will conduct an assessment of the export readiness of the applicants, to assess the applicant company, the product/service, presence in international markets, organisation and management for internationalisation. For further information on the selection criteria, please consult our website: https://f2f-project.eu/get-involved/ For the selected SMEs, an agreement will be signed between the corresponding Cluster and the beneficiary SME detailing the rights and obligations of both parties. *F2F Health Matters is operated by Wagralim (BE), Valorial (FR), Clusaga (ES), InovCluster (PT) and Bioeconomy Cluster Slovakia (SK) /!\ The F2F Health Matters team has forseen 3 calls in total, meaning one for Canada (already closed), one for Japan (already closed) and one for UAE (current call). The total funding available for the 3 calls is 105 000€, after the Canada and Japan call, 37 000€ is left for Emirats.

title: European Platforms for the promotion of emerging artists
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: The European Festivals Fund for Emerging Artists – EFFEA, an initiative of the European Festivals Association, is a fund that supports collaborations between festivals from different countries. Together, these festivals provide emerging artists with a platform to develop their work and gain visibility on the international stage. EFFEA extends an open invitation for festivals to collaborate across borders and establish a network of colleagues centred around the concept of a residency. Through EFFEA, festivals join hands to foster the success of emerging artists. EFFEA's fifth call for festivals to support emerging artists is open from 1 September to 3 November 2026 . 50 residencies will be selected involving 50 emerging artists (individuals, groups or collectives) in the seat of around 150 festivals, a leading festival in collaboration with a minimum of two partner festivals each. There are two categories of residencies: 1. EFFEA Discovery: Festivals support artists at the early stages of their careers but with a strong potential to break through internationally. 40 grants of 8.000€ will be attributed to this category. 2. EFFEA Springboard : Festivals support artists already established in their own country and ready to develop their careers internationally. 10 grants of 15.000€ will be attributed to this category. Eligibility criteria The partnership must represent at least 3 festivals from 3 eligible countries (1 leading festival and 2 partner festivals). Both leading and partner festivals must exist for at least one edition. Both leading and partner festivals must be registered on www. FestivalFinder.eu before submitting their application. A festival may apply for one grant as a leading festival and is eligible to apply for multiple grants as a partner festival. Proposed artists may be individual artists, collectives, companies, ensembles, or groups of any age and nationality. Artists must have either nationality or legal residence in one of the eligible countries. Eligible Countries Leading festivals and artists should have their official address in one of the following eligible countries: Albania, Armenia, Austria, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Georgia, Greece, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Kosovo, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Montenegro, Moldova, Netherlands, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Tunisia, Ukraine. Festivals with their official address from the following countries are allowed to participate as partner festivals only : Israel, Palestine, Switzerland, Turkey, and the UK. Artists from these countries can also be proposed. Eligible disciplines Festivals and artists work in one or more of the following artistic disciplines: Architecture, Ballet, Contemporary Dance, Circus, Design/ Applied arts, Digital arts, Film, Folklore and folk arts, Heritage, Interdisciplinary, Literature, Music, Opera, Street Art, Theatre, Photography/ Video, Puppetry, Sculpture, Painting. Conditions and Selection Criteria The start and end dates of the residency must fall within the implementation period. This means that the residency start date must be no earlier than 1 January 2027 , and the end date must be no later than 31 December 2027 . If applicants start the residency earlier or end it later, any costs related to the extended period must not be included in the budget submitted to EFFEA. Submitted proposals will be assessed for eligibility by the EFA team. All eligible proposals will be evaluated by the EFFEA Jury, composed of members with diverse profiles in terms of artistic disciplines, geographies, backgrounds, gender, age, and, above all, with knowledge of the arts field. The selection criteria assume that: The residency is relevant for the artists, festivals and audiences. It will have an impact on the artists’ careers. It offers a market to artists even beyond the residency period (longer term). The budget is built on the principle of fair remuneration towards the artists at all stages (stay, rehearsal time and payment, fees, etc.). The topics of today focus on diversity, sustainability (ecological, cultural, artistic, economic and social), digital tools and inclusion. These can be cited as motivation and will be considered in evaluating the quality of the residency. Submission The leading festival must submit the application online via the EFFEA website . Applications cannot be submitted in any other way. The leading festival will be asked to fill in: General information about leading festival/ organisation. Information about the proposed artists, including short biographies and links (text and/or audiovisual). General information about the partner festivals. Motivation for supporting the artists and establishing the partnership for the residency. Letter of intent with the artists (template available for download). Letter of intent with the partner festivals (template available for download). A detailed budget form (template available to download). The Leading Festivals must Upload and sign all required documents (including the budget and letters of intent with the artists and the partner festivals). Ensure that the proposed residency dates fall within the eligible implementation period. Ensure that the proposed artists meet the EFFEA eligibility criteria regarding previous participation. Artists who received a Discovery grant through a previous EFFEA Call remain eligible for a Springboard residency under Call #5. Applications will be evaluated in November 2026. Applicants will be notified of the results by email in December 2026.

title: Supporting Ukrainian artists and cultural organisations to co-create/showcase
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: The IZOLYATSIA Foundation (UA) and Malý Berlín (SK), together with Trans Europe Halles (SE), announce the second call for proposals for the co-creation funding of international cooperation projects. The objective of the call is to support co-creation between Ukrainian artists and cultural organisations and their peers from Creative Europe countries on the topic of resilience. Funding will be available for co-creation projects involving at least one Ukrainian partner and a partner from another Creative Europe participating country. Each partner is expected to play a role of comparable weight in the project — whether through creative input, management responsibilities, or audience development. All creative sectors are eligible, with the exception of the audio-visual sector. Each co-creation project must include a public presentation in the locality of every participating partner. Purpose of the call: To develop and present an international co-creation on the topic of resilience, in any artistic/cultural sector except audio-visual. To carry out at least two local presentations (one/locality, including in Ukraine) Budget: — Total funding available 187,500€ — Amounts per grant: Up to 25,000€, covering up to 90% of project costs. — Applicants are expected and required to provide the rest of the total project budget as a contribution. — Expected number of grants 7-10 Eligible applicants: Organisations active in the field of arts and culture established in a Creative Europe country ( EU countries , non-EU countries ). For Ukraine, they must be registered in a zone effectively controlled by the Ukrainian government . Projects must include at least two partners from at least two countries, of which one is Ukraine. Individual artists and freelancers cannot apply directly; they must take part through an eligible organisation acting as a project partner. List of activities that are eligible for financial support: — All activities necessary for the co-creation project implementation and development. — Presentation of the co-creation in the locality of each project partner. — Travel related to organisational, rehearsal, artistic, presentation purposes. Duration of the project: — project duration period: up to 7 months within the indicative implementation window of February–August 2027; — earliest start of the project after the signature of the grant agreement. Technical eligibility criteria: all required attachments (as described in the Application Procedure below) are uploaded to the platform in separate files and in the formats specified for this call; all required attachments are uploaded to the platform following standard templates that can be downloaded on the platform; all required attachments are readable, accessible, and printable; all the project partners meet the eligibility conditions specified for this call; the registration of all the project partners meets the conditions specified for this call; the application form is complete and contains all the requested information; the total subgrant amount requested in the budget is within the maximum subgrant amounts determined for this call; the total project partners contribution meets the conditions specified for this call; project implementation period is within the project implementation period defined for this call; the start of project implementation meets the conditions specified for this call. Selection criteria: Relevance: — relevance of the project to the objectives of the call; — relevance of potential co-creation to act as a basis for intercultural dialogue. Quality: — quality of extent to which cross-cutting issues (digital, green, inclusion) are addressed, including barrier-free access to project results; — quality of the partnership: the equal importance of the roles played by project partners; — quality of scale of engagement, measured by the expected audience size and number of local presentations. Impact: — Impact and the sustainability of the project, including plans and possibilities for future presentations of the co-creation. Selection procedure: Applications will first undergo a technical eligibility check by the ZMINA:Resilience team to verify that they meet all formal requirements, including admissibility and eligibility criteria. Proposals that pass this stage will then be assigned to two independent evaluators each. Evaluators will assign scores to applications. Then, the applications will be rated according to the average score. The final selection will be made by the Selection Committee, taking into account geographical, sectoral, and thematic diversity, within the available budget of the call. The application budget will be assessed for cost-effectiveness and plausibility, and may be adjusted before the grant agreement is signed. The final grant amount will be determined based on a combination of lump sum units and actual costs incurred: costs such as artist fees, travel, accommodation, and per diems are paid at the fixed unit rates listed under "Eligible costs covered by the grant" below, regardless of the exact amount spent, while costs such as equipment rental, production services, and shipping are reimbursed based on actual costs incurred. Due to the volume of applications received, the ZMINA:Resilience project team will not be able to provide individual feedback for selection decisions. All decisions are final. Application Procedure — Applications must be submitted via the IZOLYATSIA online platform no later than 04.12.2026, 23:59 Kyiv time / 22:49 Central European Time on https://platform.izolyatsia.org/en/contest/zmina-resilience-cocreation-two . — Applicant: The application shall be submitted by a single representative of the consortium/project partners (Lead Applicant). Required Documents: The application form and budget (completed directly on the platform), Supporting documents regarding capacity, eligibility, and admissibility. The following must be uploaded to the platform in .pdf format separately for each partner: A scanned copy of the Letter of Guarantee , completed and signed by the head of the applicant organization (template available for download on the platform); Registration documents for organisation registered in Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine: national registration documents with English translation in case the document is issued in another language. Registration documents for organisation from Ukraine: Full Extract from the Unified State Register of Legal Entities, Physical Persons-Entrepreneurs, and Public Formations dated on or after 5 October 2026 - in their original language. The current version of the Statutes or equivalent (if mandatory for the legal entity) – all pages: for organisation registered in Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine: with English translation in case the document is issued in another language, for organisation from Ukraine: in their original language. Language of application: The application must be submitted in English. Support: During the application period, assistance will be provided through Q&A sessions and a dedicated email helpline. Subgrant Agreement Template Funding Conditions — Financial support: 70% is disbursed upon signing the grant agreement, and the remaining amount is paid upon submission and approval of the report. — Co-financing is mandatory and must be at least 10% of the total project budget. — Double funding within the EU budget is not allowed. — All costs must be incurred after the grant agreement is signed and within the project implementation period. — Compliance with EU branding and visibility requirements is mandatory . Eligible costs covered by the grant include Daily fee for artistic work: 75€/artist/day Travel: International: 350€/return trip or Local (e.g. participation in trainings): 65€/return trip Support to green travel (in addition to the travel rate above, for one-way trips over 600km not made by air): 300€ Accommodation & per diem: 75€/overnight Visa cost, if needed: 80€ Shipping/Transport (of equipment), incl. insurance: at cost; Supplies & equipment (for equipment depreciation costs only): at cost; Services required for project implementation (production, rental of equipment, rental of space for project events, etc.): at cost; Communication, marketing and documentation: at cost. Management and administration costs: Max. 20% of the overall project budget (grant amount plus own contribution/co-financing combined). Estimated dates: — Launch of the Call for Proposals: 5 October 2026 — Deadline for Submission of Applications: until 23:59 4December 2026 (Kyiv time) — Evaluation Period: December 2026 — Announcement of Results: January 2027 — Signing of Grant Agreements: February 2027 — Implementation of Selected Projects: February 2027 – August 2027 (each project runs up to 7 months within this window, depending on its grant agreement signing date)

title: Fostering Ukrainians’ access to culture and cultural heritage
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Culture Helps Solidarity - Open Call for Individual Grant Sixth round, 12 October - 26 October 2026 Culture Helps Solidarity supports arts and culture professionals from Ukraine to sustain creativity, resilience, and community connection during and after the war. Running until 2028, the project combines three grant schemes - individual grants, thematic project grants, and collaboration grants - with a rich programme of mentoring, learning, and peer exchange. The project is co-funded through the Creative Europe programme and implemented by the European Cultural Foundation (Amsterdam), an independent foundation fostering European belonging through culture; together with Insha Osvita (Kyiv), a Ukrainian NGO and professional learning community developing educational and cultural programmes; zusa (Berlin), an international NGO fostering collaboration and collective learning for social and cultural change; and the VETERANKA Movement (Kyiv), Ukraine's leading community of women veterans advocating for women's rights, leadership, and reintegration. The Individual Grants provide direct, flexible support to cultural professionals in and from Ukraine who are working - often voluntarily - with displaced people and refugees, veterans and vulnerable communities, in Ukraine or in any of the Creative Europe (CE) countries (which include the 27 EU Member States and more countries participating in Creative Europe ). These personal care grants are designed to offer quick and accessible assistance for strengthening the personal wellbeing, resilience and mental health of cultural professionals and creatives, enabling them to continue their crucial cultural, community-based work in extremely challenging circumstances. These grants are not designed to cover costs related to project delivery or implementation. This is the sixth call in the series of rolling application rounds, opening approximately every six weeks. Across the 2026-2028 project period, we anticipate 10–14 such cycles. In each cycle, approximately 7 to 10 grants of up to EUR 1,200 will be disbursed. WHO IS IT FOR? This call seeks to support individual professionals in need for individual wellbeing care who work in arts, culture or community-based cultural activities and: support displaced Ukrainians, both inside Ukraine and across Creative Europe countries; play a meaningful and publicly relevant role for maintaining cultural production, artistic creation or community life in Ukraine or in Creative Europe countries; work with veterans and vulnerable groups; seek urgent personal wellbeing support that will enable them to continue their work, creative practice, and engagement with their communities; have been personally affected by war, displacement, and/or traumatic working conditions. WHAT DO WE OFFER? We offer up to €1,200 (including taxes if applicable) per individual, disbursed as a one-off contribution. The grant may be used strictly for personal mental health and wellbeing support and may not be directed to third parties, to project implementation or organisational costs. Eligible activities include: Psychotherapy or psychological counselling; Trauma-informed coaching or emotional (group) support sessions; Restorative care or rehabilitation stays (e.g., sanatorium treatment, wellness programmes, retreats); Visit to cultural institutions and events (tickets to museums, theatres, cinemas, concerts, etc.); Participation in master classes or workshops (art therapy) and materials for participation in them, if necessary; Other justified wellbeing-oriented services that directly support the applicant’s resilience. The grant may not be used for: psychiatric consultations or medical mental‑health treatment (including any expenses that involve medical care, diagnosis); purchase of medication or medical devices (even if prescribed by a doctor); purchase of material assets (tools, household items, equipment, etc., consumables for work, etc.); payment of rent for premises (residential or commercial, non-residential); tuition fees, other training costs (formal or informal); invasive interventions (surgical operations, cosmetic procedures, dental interventions, etc.); streaming platform subscriptions; consultations with doctors of alternative medical practice; strictly humanitarian needs or cost-of-living support. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Individual grants are strictly dedicated to individuals, who: are aged 18 and above; reside in Ukraine or have fled from Ukraine to one of the Creative Europe countries (which include the 27 EU Member States and more countries participating in Creative Europe ); artists, cultural managers, or activists and volunteers working with displaced persons in Ukraine, or with displaced persons and refugees from Ukraine in one of the Creative Europe countries, veterans and vulnerable groups; submit a complete application form in either Ukrainian or English language. SELECTION CRITERIA AND PROCESS: Relevance of professional context – Does the applicant demonstrate a convincing role within their artistic, cultural, or cultural-community environment, and clearly explain the relevance of their engagement through artistic practice, cultural production, and/or culture-based community initiatives? Personal wellbeing relevance – Is the requested support clearly related to maintaining or strengthening the applicant's personal wellbeing and resilience at this stage of their life and work? Public and community impact – Is the applicant able to convincingly demonstrate their continued contribution to arts, culture, and/or culture-based community life, generating benefits for the communities, audiences, or cultural environments with which they engage? Coherence and feasibility of the planned use of funds - Are the requested activities realistic and eligible to the purpose of supporting the applicant's wellbeing? Following an eligibility check, applications will be assessed by external advisors who are familiar with the cultural sector and the current context in Ukraine. Final decisions will be made by the consortium partners, who review the recommendations to ensure consistency and budgetary balance. 7 to 10 applications will be awarded per round. TIMELINE: 12 October 2026 sixth call for proposals open 14 October 2026 info session 26 October 2026 call closed End of November 2026 proposals assessed and selected 12 January 2027 seventh call for proposals open HOW TO APPLY? The submission deadline for proposals is Monday, 26 th of October 2026, 13:00 Amsterdam time/ 14:00 Kyiv time. You can find more information and useful application tips, as well as complete the application form, including the budget section via this link: https://culture-of-solidarity-fund.grantplatform.com/ .

The upcoming application rounds will each be open for two weeks, followed by a three/four-weeks assessment period. To ensure high-quality assessment and an effective allocation of support, each round can accommodate up to 170 applications. Should you have further questions, please contact us at chs@culturalfoundation.eu.

title: Perform EU
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: Perform Europe is a funding scheme offering EUR 1.4 million for performing arts collaborations across all 41 Creative Europe countries. Perform Europe supports partnership proposals which reinvent the way we tour across borders. The highly successful Perform Europe pilot (2020–2022) and second edition (2023–2026), was coordinated by a Consortium of six organisations; five major performing arts networks, IETM - International network for contemporary performing arts, European Festivals Association (EFA), European Dance Development Network (EDN), Circostrada, Pearle* - Live Performance Europe together with the research organisation IDEA Consult. Co-funded by the European Union, Perform Europe has granted a total of €3.5 million to 61 cross-border macro-projects involving 272 partners. Together, they have toured over 80 artistic works across 41 countries, reaching new audiences and testing innovative approaches to inclusion, sustainability and cooperation. Building on these achievements, the third and final edition of Perform Europe under the current Creative Europe programme (2021-2028) will continue to explore, together with the performing arts sector, how cross-border touring can become fairer, greener and more inclusive, while further consolidating the knowledge, partnerships and practices developed through the programme. By the end of this third edition, Perform Europe will have supported at least 86 cross-border touring projects in total, building a substantial body of experience and knowledge that continues to strengthen the European performing arts ecosystem. Keywords: performing arts, theatre, dance, performance, circus, outdoor arts, puppetry, interdisciplinary, change-makers, inclusion, diversity, fight against climate change, sustainability, fairness, cross-border mobility, innovation Do you have an innovative idea that resonates with these keywords? Read on! PRIORITIES OF PERFORM EUROPE Proposals are submitted by collaboration partnerships of performing arts professionals and organisations. Partners should work on their proposal together. This is a call to the sector to create partnerships and propose impactful ideas that can generate real change via two main priorities: INCLUSION & DIVERSITY FIGHT AGAINST CLIMATE CHANGE Each proposal should choose one of the above main priorities to focus on, while still taking into account and implementing measures related to the second priority. In addition, all proposals should aim for quality and innovation, be built on fair practices, and are encouraged to promote collaboration across different regions within the 41 Creative Europe countries. Read more about the priorities in our guidelines below. CONDITIONS OF THE CALL The open call was launched on 23 June 2026. We invite you now to build partnerships, jointly develop proposals, and submit them through our website before 22 October 2026, 23:59 CEST. FUNDING Perform Europe will grant EUR 1.4 million to at least 25 partnerships . Partnerships can apply for grants in three categories: EUR 15,000 - small grant EUR 25,000 - medium grant EUR 55,000 - large grant In addition to the requested grant category, partnerships can request top-ups to address the sustainability and accessibility needs of their proposal. Each partnership may request any combination of the available top-ups, up to a maximum total top-up request of EUR 5,000 per proposal. The maximum granted amount, including top-ups, will be EUR 60,000, a requirement set by the funder, the European Union. Of the total funding, 5% will be allocated to proposals which involve a partnership with Ukrainian partners or support initiatives for the Ukrainian performing arts sector. WHO CAN APPLY Any organisation and professional working in the performing arts, and legally based in one of the Creative Europe Countries ( 27 EU member states plus 14 non-EU Participating Countries ). PARTNERSHIP REQUIREMENTS Proposals are submitted by partnerships. Each partnership must consist of a minimum of three partners from a minimum of three Creative Europe countries. Each proposal must include at least one performing arts work (excluding live music and opera) to be presented in a minimum of three different Creative Europe countries. Important to note: Perform Europe will not cover production costs for new creations: proposals are supposed to include a finished artistic work (finished production or an artistic concept ready to be applied and presented in different contexts). Looking for partners? Use the Matchmaking Platform on the Perform Europe website to join a community of over 2,300 performing arts organisations and professionals from 41 countries looking to make changes in the sector. TIMELINE 23 June 2026: Launch of the open call 22 October 2026 23:59 CEST: Deadline for submitting proposals January 2027: Announcement of selected partnerships 1 March 2027: Selected proposals start touring 31 January 2028: Selected proposals finish touring During the open call period, Perform Europe will organise help desk sessions, information, promotion and knowledge-sharing events regarding the open call. Check out the events calendar for more details. GET READY TO APPLY Read the full open call guidelines below Register and apply on the Perform Europe website Apply before Thursday, 22 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST APPLICATION DOCUMENTS Perform Europe Open Call and Guidelines PDF-version of the digital application form Budget template Cooperation agreement template Co-financing commitment letter template Frequently Asked Questions IMPORTANT RESOURCES Perform Europe Conversation Starter for building partnerships and designing your proposal Perform Europe Guidebook and Resources for inspiration and research Help Desk Sessions – for all your questions The Matchmaking Platform – for finding partners To stay updated about all events and important news, visit our website at performeurope.eu , subscribe to our newsletter and follow us on social media @PerformEurope.

title: Circulation of European literary works
description: Expected Impact: The action is expected to support around 40 projects, implemented either by a single entity (mono-beneficiary) or by a consortium of organisations (multi-beneficiary). Objective: This action will support projects that will translate, publish, distribute, and promote European Literature. This action complements the other Creative Europe support actions to the book and publishing sector, such as reading promotion through the European Authors Day to younger audiences and the European Union Prize for Literature targeting European emerging authors. The works covered by this call for proposals are European literary works , such as novels, short stories, theatre plays and radio plays, poetry, literary reportage, comic books as well as children and youth literature. For the purposes of this call for proposals ‘ European literary works’ refers to works written by authors who are linked to an eligible country (Creative Europe countries)[EU Member States (including overseas countries and territories (OCTs)) + non-EU countries: listed EEA countries and countries associated to the Creative Europe Programme ( list of participating countries )], by their nationality or place of residence, or who are recognised as belonging to the European literary heritage. Themes and priorities In line with the current cultural policy priorities, applicants should propose projects contributing to: 1. EU Overarching priorities: Applicants must describe in their application how, in the design and implementation of their projects, they intend to contribute to the EU's Overarching priorities. 2. The following specific priorities: Increasing the transnational circulation and the diversity of European literary works, notably through the translation, publication, distribution and promotion of works written in less translated languages; Promoting reading and the linguistic and cultural diversity of European literature to a large audience, through increasing discoverability of the literary works supported; Supporting the profession of literary translator, in line with the principles of good working conditions and fair remuneration publishers should ensure that the names of the translators appear visibly in published books, and preferably on the cover, and that the source language is also clearly mentioned; Increasing the competitiveness of the book sector by encouraging cooperation between different actors within the book value chain, notably between publishers, booksellers, and libraries. In addition, as part of the exceptional support to Ukraine, applicants are encouraged to propose activities facilitating the circulation of books from and/or into Ukraine, as well as their translation into or from Ukrainian. In addition, projects aimed at providing books in the Ukrainian language to Ukrainian refugees and displaced people will be encouraged. In this context, the printing in Ukrainian of (non-translated) Ukrainian books will be eligible. To support the profession of literary translator, in accordance with the principles of good working conditions and fair remuneration, it is recommended that between 20 and 30%[This percentage will apply to novel literary genre.] of the total project budget is allocated to the remuneration of translators and that translators are given recognition and visibility, particularly being credited, preferably on the cover page. To preserve the profession of literary translator, and the quality of translation, machine translation is excluded from this call. Publishers will have to sign contracts with professional human literary translators, and the data about the chosen translators must be clearly indicated in the overview of translations in the Creative Europe Database (see section 5. Admissibility and documents). In this regard, publishers should respect national standards and follow best practices, referring to and using, the ‘Translators on the cover’ report and, as an example, the ‘Guidelines for fair translation contracts’ drawn up by CEATL . Scope: Translation, publication, promotion, and distribution activities as well as activities addressing the themes and priorities described above. More specifically: Activities relating to literary works to be translated, published and promoted, as part of a robust publishing strategy and an effective distribution plan. Activities aimed at facilitating collaboration between the various stakeholders in the book and publishing value chain: authors, translators, publishers, distributors, booksellers, libraries, literary events and festivals. The proposed activities should be grouped, in the application form (part B), in coherent work packages. Each work package must have a corresponding list of activities, deliverables, milestones, and critical risks.
